title: RIGBY
subtitle: Low-cost mobile bimanual manipulator for accessible household assistance.
description: A final-year robotics system combining a mobile base, asymmetric bimanual arms, imitation learning from demonstration, and a web, touch, and voice interface for non-expert users.

sections.title: System
sections.body: RIGBY was designed as an accessible research platform for household assistance: a mobile base, two low-cost arms, calibrated cameras, and a task interface that lets a user request or demonstrate actions.

sections.title: Contribution
sections.body: The work covered mechanical integration, dataset recording, imitation-learning training, robot control, and the user-facing GUI that ties the system together.

title: Smart Robot Assistant
subtitle: Friendly companion robot for adaptive support and play.
description: An interactive robotic companion built to aid children with disabilities through game-playing support, computer vision, and approachable human-robot interaction.

sections.title: Intent
sections.body: The project explored how a robot can be useful without feeling clinical: expressive enough for play, structured enough for assistance, and adaptive enough for different user needs.

sections.title: Build
sections.body: The system combined sensing, control, and interface design so the robot could respond to the task context and support a child through a guided activity.

title: TFLbot
subtitle: A helping hand around underground transport networks.
description: A human-centred robotics prototype exploring whether a mobile Pepper assistant can reduce the friction of underground travel through autonomous guidance, speech, visual feedback, multilingual interaction, and British Sign Language support.

specs.label: Stack
specs.value: ROS2 Humble, NAOqi bridge, Flask UI

specs.label: Perception
specs.value: Orbbec RGB-D, RPLIDAR, speech, and BSL cues

specs.label: Result
specs.value: Compared no aid, static aid, and mobile aid conditions

sections.title: Robot
sections.body: TFLbot used Pepper as the public-facing robot, then extended the platform with an Orbbec Femto Bolt RGB-D camera, RPLIDAR A2M12, ReSpeaker microphone array, Jetson Orin Nano, Raspberry Pi 5, and custom mounting so the robot could perceive users, speak, gesture, and move as a coherent guide.

sections.title: Task
sections.body: The task was framed around accessible underground navigation: help passengers request route information, receive TFL-style status updates, choose languages, and interact through speech, tablet feedback, or BSL mode rather than relying only on static signs or staff availability.

sections.title: Control
sections.body: The control architecture used ROS2 Humble with a NAOqi bridge running on the Jetson to process and publish speech, wheel, and upper-body movement commands. A Flask UI inside a ROS2 wrapper connected user commands to the bridge, while LLM output was published as structured task-manager messages for speech, gesture, and navigation behaviours.

sections.title: Results
sections.body: The evaluation compared no aid, static aid, and mobile aid conditions using task completion time and workload-style measures. The results made the trade-off visible: robotic guidance can improve clarity and accessibility, but mobility and interaction timing must be controlled carefully so assistance does not become additional overhead.

title: Adaptive Chess Coach
subtitle: Robotic arm that turns virtual chess into a physical assisted game.
description: A robotic chess coach that transfers virtual moves to a real board, provides real-time help, and adjusts game difficulty according to user needs.

sections.title: Experience
sections.body: The system connects software gameplay to physical manipulation, letting the user play on a tangible board while the robot executes, demonstrates, or assists with moves.

sections.title: Engineering
sections.body: The main challenge was coordinating board-state interpretation, safe arm motion, and assistance logic into one reliable interaction loop.

title: Prompt-Aware Web Scraper
subtitle: Embedding-based web discovery from natural-language prompts.
description: An automated NLP tool that uses text embeddings to identify and scrape relevant Google search results from a user prompt.

sections.title: Pipeline
sections.body: The scraper converts a prompt into an embedding search problem, ranks candidate results by semantic relevance, and extracts the pages most likely to matter.

sections.title: Value
sections.body: It turns search from a brittle keyword exercise into a more intent-aware collection workflow.

title: Market Making Algorithm
subtitle: Competition strategy ranked third at Imperial.
description: An algorithmic trading model for an Optiver-style market-making competition, ranking 3rd out of roughly 100 participants at Imperial College London.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: The algorithm balanced spread capture, inventory risk, and changing market information under competition constraints.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: The final model placed third in the field, with performance driven by disciplined quoting and careful response to price signals.
